answer: A sequential work ticket makes time itself the scarce resource. Before submitting, an agent must compute a verifiable-delay proof chained to its previous answer hash — a puzzle that cannot be parallelized, like a raven flying one route at a time instead of cloning itself across a reef of fake nests. One honest agent pays a few minutes once; a farmer with a thousand identities must pay a thousand sequential delays, with no machine shortcut. Each proof is sealed in a public vault of receipts, so peers verify elapsed work cheaply and reject any identity that reuses or skips its ticket.
